record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Degree partition for triangle-free K2,3-free graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a triangle-free graph with no K_{2,3} subgraph, and let a and b be integer-valued functions on V(G) such that a(x) >= 2, b(x) >= 2, and d(x) >= a(x) + b(x) - 1 for every vertex x. Must V(G) have a partition (A, B) such that every x in A has at least a(x) neighbors inside A and every y in B has at least b(y) neighbors inside B?

evidence.quote: Theorem 4.3[47] Let G be a triangle-free graph in which no two quadrilaterals share edges, and a, b two integral functions on V (G) such that a(x) ≥ 2 and b(x) ≥ 2 for each vertex x of G. If d(x) ≥ a(x) + b(x) − 1 for each vertex x of G, then G admits a partition (A, B) such that dA(x) ≥ a(x) for each x ∈ A, and dB(y) ≥ b(y) for each y ∈ B.
It would be nice if someone can strengthen Theorem 4.3 to triangle-free and K2,3-free graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph that is triangle-free (contains no $K_3$ subgraph) and $K_{2,3}$-free (contains no subgraph isomorphic to the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,3}$). For each vertex $x \in V$, let $d(x)$ denote its degree in $G$. Suppose $a, b : V \to \mathbb{Z}$ are functions such that for every $x \in V$:
\[ a(x) \ge 2, \quad b(x) \ge 2, \quad d(x) \ge a(x) + b(x) - 1. \]
For a subset $S \subseteq V$ and $x \in S$, let $d_S(x)$ denote the number of neighbors of $x$ that lie in $S$.

Determine whether $V$ necessarily admits a partition $V = A \sqcup B$ such that
\[ d_A(x) \ge a(x) \text{ for every } x \in A, \quad \text{and} \quad d_B(y) \ge b(y) \text{ for every } y \in B. \]
artifact.status_search_result: A related result by Hou, Ma, Yu, and Zhang (Discrete Mathematics, 2018) on partitions of $K_{2,3}$-free graphs under degree constraints establishes $g(s,t;K_{2,3}) \le s+t$ for constants $s,t \ge 2$, which is one larger than the bound asked for. The strengthening to triangle-free and $K_{2,3}$-free graphs with the sharper degree condition $d(x) \ge a(x)+b(x)-1$ and variable functions $a,b$ does not appear to have a confirmed resolution in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: On partitions of K2,3-free graphs under degree constraints
status_evidence.snippet: g(s, t; K_{2,3}) ≤ s + t for s, t ≥ 2, where g(s,t;H) is the least integer g such that any H-free graph with minimum degree at least g admits a partition into two sets whose induced subgraphs have minimum degrees at least s and t respectively.
status_evidence.claim: A bound of s+t (one weaker than the conjectured s+t-1) is known for K_{2,3}-free graphs without the triangle-free assumption.

status_evidence.title: 10 problems for partitions of triangle-free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A list of open problems concerning partitions of triangle-free graphs under degree constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent surveys still list partition problems of this type as open.
